report:
Reassessed the complete precedence claim and all three evidence entries. The ordinary resolver association supplies the complete resolve/mod.rs. resolve_path checks lexical ribs for a lone relative segment (and the receiver self special form), while other path forms enter module resolution. Namespace is carried through lookup, intermediate segments use the type namespace, and final segments retain the requested namespace. Normal module resolution searches named items/imports before globs; flexible lookup then tries extern, edition standard, and language preludes. Anchored lookup selects self, parent, crate-root or external modules; qualified external lookup uses named exported children. Named-use aliases and recursive glob resolution preserve namespace and the in-flight module/name/namespace key terminates cycles. This is ordered lookup, not an unordered global pool. The explicit T::Item integration FIXME is not evidence that such type-dependent paths work.

The sole ordinary test transitive_local_globs_resolve_and_glob_cycles_terminate supplies a b/c glob cycle and a transitive a import. Its body requires resolved Item to be an ADT without arguments, checks its name, and requires Missing to lower to Ty::Error. These assertions meaningfully cover successful transitive imports and recovery/termination for a missing name through cycles, but do not establish all precedence dimensions. Captured fixture helpers create and populate a Rust2021 root module; they do not introduce hidden behavioral assertions.

The second test, sage_meta::todo::resolution_lookup_precedence, explicitly defers the complete matrix: lexical shadowing, independent type/value/macro namespaces, qualified versus unqualified paths, renamed imports, cycles and edition preludes. Its empty body is not coverage. Completing that deferral requires concrete competing-name fixtures, expected selected identities, qualified ancestry/external import cases and edition-aware prelude fixtures; the existing cycle example supplies only one part. I accept the existing declared test gap, including these remaining precedence scenarios, without treating them as implemented-and-tested. No N/A evidence exists.

Baseline: personally compared all three historical implementation/test source snapshots to current files and verified exact byte equality, and verified the historical claim is unchanged. The historical rationale remains sufficient for its narrow cycle evidence and explicit matrix deferral after this independent reassessment. Source inspection and captured fixture context support this report; I executed review start/read and the byte comparisons, not behavioral tests or a build. The coordinator separately reports a successful build and 321 sage-meta tests; those are not my execution evidence. No source edits or additional claims of full coverage.
